overall_assessment.realism: The samples demonstrate a high level of realism, incorporating detailed technical metadata such as SMTP transaction logs, domain registration data, URL analyses, and linguistic features consistent with real-world phishing campaigns. The use of domain-in-subdomain obfuscation, newly registered domains, and personalized message content aligns well with contemporary phishing tactics. The inclusion of plausible user agent strings and email authentication results (DKIM, SPF, DMARC) further enhances authenticity. However, some domain names and registrar details, while plausible, could be cross-checked against known registrars for absolute realism.
overall_assessment.consistency: The dataset maintains strong consistency across samples, with uniform structure and comprehensive coverage of relevant fields such as scenario description, technical data, indicators, detection methods, and MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Each entry consistently includes email or SMS headers, body content, URL and domain analyses, and linguistic features. The formatting of timestamps, IP addresses, and URLs adheres to standard conventions. Minor inconsistencies include slight variations in the depth of detail for certain fields (e.g., some SMTP logs are more verbose), but overall schema adherence is solid.
suggestions: Standardize the level of detail in SMTP transaction logs across all samples to ensure uniformity.
Validate domain registrar names and WHOIS data against real-world registries to enhance credibility.
Include explicit schema versioning or metadata to facilitate dataset maintenance and evolution.
Add more varied user agent strings to reflect a broader range of devices and browsers.
Incorporate additional contextual metadata such as geolocation of IP addresses or time zone consistency checks.
Consider adding sample response or mitigation actions to enrich the dataset's practical utility.
Ensure all timestamps are consistently in UTC or clearly specify time zones to avoid ambiguity.
